Cigarette Investigative

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Where did your illegal cigarettes come from? We go right back to the beginning and bring you the behind the scenes of the cigarette wars.

Unique Selling Point:
We have a source who has exclusively given us evidence of the illicit cigarette market. The source cannot be identified, however all information has been sent to exec management. We will uncover the payments to presidents and their family members - then also how the smuggling industry began. We will touch on how the smuggling rings work - how they originally pay off sars/border officials to import from zim and bring superlink trucks, then fly in product, and now round trip or ghost the cigarettes. We'll show how the current players - originally smugglers have now been legitimized...

Summary:
We'll talk to JVL about what happened to him when he got too close, how his safe was cracked open to get documents etc and we'll give him cigarettes we have in our possession that were not bought by us, but that were bought by consumers during lockdown and he'll tell us about them.

Then we'll talk to snkyers about the import/export industry in SA, the stats and she'll explain what's happening now with the exports. She has her won theories how people are currently getting cigarettes.

Then we will look at the current illicit market and how people are getting them from shopping centres etc...

Case Study:
X Cigarette smugger
Adriano Mazzotti Cigarette manufacturer
Yusuf Kajee cigarette manufacturer
Edward Zuma Presidents son
Mandlakazi British American Tobacco

Expert:
Mr. Johan van Loggerenberg ex SARS
Mr. Telita Snykers Cigarette expert

Locations:
Johannesburg
Pretoria
KZN

Hidden Camera: No

Legal: Yes
Reason for legal: it's the most lucrative industry

Script:


Die-hard smokers are so desperate for a drag, they’ll pay almost anything.
UPSOUND: im counting out my cash for my cigarettes which is R2000, but is usually R300.
...this delivery comes disguised as a present…other smokers innovate…
Upsound: We don’t throw our stompies away etc look at the amount of tobacco still left…”
Under lockdown, Minister of Cooperative Governance and Traditional Affairs Dr Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma enforced a prolonged GOVERNMENT smoking ban citing health concerns. But it’s resulted in forcing smokers to break the law to feed their nicotine addiction.
Woman: If there’s 10 ppl, they smoke 1 cigarette because why? Each person must given R1 to smoke that cigarette.
JVL: if you’re going to be a smoker, don't buy things that fund organized crime because if you do that, don't complain if people come and break into your homes, because you're paying them.
If anyone knows about organized criminals it’s Johann Van Loggerenberg who is a former South African Revenue Service tax and customs fraud investigator who took on the illicit tobacco industry.
JVL: The ban is a complete failure. within 70 days the ban has pushed in excess of 2 billion rand into the pockets of by and large organised crime syndicates.
Van Loggerenberg is referring to the supply chain of smugglers and illicit traders. We ventured one evening to meet a veteran smuggler Mr X, who made millions from illegally importing Zimbabwean cigarettes.
Mr X: Before the lock down they were selling a carton of 10 packs for R70, currently they're selling for R400 rand.
He says the ban has seen obscene profits for smugglers and other criminals in the cigarette supply chain. The game, he says, has always been to avoid the VAT and high sin tax on cigarettes...
If a pack of 20 costs R2 to make, the tax comes to R17.
BUT if a cigarette is exported, the manufacturer doesn’t pay tax or can claim it back. There are 5 ways to avoid tax according to experts and smugglers:
1. Cross border smuggling
2. Round tripping: you export the cigarettes...and immediately smuggle them back in
3. Ghost exports: the documents say the cigarettes are exported, but they never are
4. Removal from warehouses or during transit
5.Off-radar manufacturing – factories secretly make so-called number 2 stock, often at night.
If you can avoid paying that R17 per pack, imagine how your profits will soar. That’s a massive incentive and is born out in numbers from 2018 which show that 185 million packs were unaccounted for. Various sources gave us a variety of brands sold during lockdown, which we then showed Van Loggernberg. He explains that legal brands bear a SARS stamp.
it's a dye in the shape of a diamond With the letters SAin the middle which is then uniquely numbered and provided to a registered manufacturer or importer for local consumption and taxes were paid on them. Now of course the big question is when this was manufactured was this manufactured during the lockdown period or before?
As SARS hasn’t implemented new legislation that would allow illicit packs to be traced, the diamond stamp during lockdown becomes meaningless.
Jvl: I cannot imagine what went through their minds when they banned the trade in cigarettes and not put into place additional measures to deal with the very predictable consequences.
Then, a month into the ban, the government allowed local cigarette manufacturers to export cigarettes.
Snykers: so in effect it created a loophole local companies could continue producing ostensibly for the export market. And then probably exporting some of those volumes but divert some of those volumes and sell them on the local market.
A former SARS Lawyer, Telita Snyckers has investigated international cigarette smuggling and discovered that both large and small brands are available for sale under lockdown. This does not mean the manufacturers were breaking the rules – the illicit trade in these brands could be the result of criminal activity in the supply chain.
We were given these locally-manufactured brands... like Dunhill from BAT, the British American Tobacco Group, which has operations across 6 continents and a factory in South Africa...and also smaller manufacturers that sell cheaper brands. These include Amalgamated Tobacco Manufacturers, or ATM, which operates from Pietermartizburg and sells brands like Malimbo and Johannesburg-based Carnilinx, with among other brands, JFK.
A research unit that studies cigarette tax at the University of Cape Town surveyed 12,000 smokers and found the market share had shifted during lockdown. 60% of cigarettes sold before lockdown were BAT brands - in May, of the illicit cigarettes sold 24% are BAT brands, 10% are Carnilinx brands, which is up from 2% and ATM’s brands are up from 0.4% to 2%. Then this week the UCT research unit updated the numbers from June, surveying 23,000 smokers. It found that of the illicit cigarettes sold now, BATs brands decreased to 9%, while Carnilinx brands increased to 14% and ATM’s brands rose to 10%.
Also in June, the tobacco industry took the government to court demanding the rationale for the ban. The court found that, for health reasons, the ban was rational and necessary during the pandemic and that cigarettes were not “essential”. ATM, CARNILINX AND BAT are challenging the ban.
JVL: The fact that we are told that if we want to know the reasons we need to go to court is also problematic because you know when government defends itself we fund them through taxpayers money
But Mr X, for one, finds the continuation of the ban suspicious, saying behind closed doors tobacco players have always had close ties with government officials and politicians.
Mr X: There’s too many loopholes and lots of corruption within the industry...and everybody is politically connected.
This is why some suggest Minister Dlamini-Zuma is benefitting from an alleged close relationship with Carnilinx director Adriano Mazzotti who was alleged to have paid money towards her presidential campaign -- an allegation both have denied. But now Mazzotti’s past is again being dug up, as he had admitted to smuggling in 2014, in order to cut a deal with SARS, when the agency went after him for tax evasion.
JVL:it describes ‘How he met an official who gave him documents and he paid for that which is a bribe - that SARS official is still within SARS to this day. He describes how 40 tons per week smuggled into the country.
The plea deal fell through and Mazzotti was never convicted.
He declined an interview now – saying he’s not benefitting in any way from the illicit trade and he can’t be held responsible for illegal traders. He questioned the credibility of both UCT reports that show a rise in CARNILINX brands sold.He says Carnilinx wasn’t consulted; the numbers are unreliable and not based on a nationwide market, and the ban has severely impacted Carnilinx. He questioned the relevance of having his private tax affairs aired.
Mr X insists that Minister Damini-Zuma’s former husband's family deserve scrutiny.
A tobacco insider shared information with SARS in 2013 that funds from tobacco smuggling were being channelled to fund upgrades to the Nkandla household, and former president Jacob Zuma’s family. Some of those documents have NOW been entrusted to us by Mr X. One of the alleged smugglers is the director of ATM - Yusuf Kajee.
JVL: Mr. Kajee, to use his terminology. He says you know um he was half pregnant. Meaning that he ran a legitimate factory but he also ran something else.
That “something else” is said to be a smuggling operation that brought in tobacco from Zimbabwe. Over several years the company’s paperwork was adjusted and it became known as Delta Tobacco, run by Kajee and his business partner Azeem Carim.
SITTING WITH DOCUMENTS: DELTA TOBACCO'S ACCOUNT RAN THROUGH ANOTHER COMPANY CALLED ROYAL SONNIC, - THESE ACCOUNTS COME DIRECTLY FROM THEIR ACCOUNT MANAGERS AND ARE SENT TO KAJEE AND CARIM EVERYDAY.
X: That company was making payments to the zumas Including payments made in cash to Nkandla, and these payments were made for political protection.
Masa: How much are we talking here?
X: R150,000 a month.
The documents reveal monthly payments of R30,000 to Jacob Zuma’s son, Edward, plus flights and BMW X5 car instalments.
THE ACCOUNTS SHOW BRIBES: R380,000 TO TRANSPORTERS AND CLEARING AGENTS, R150,000 FOR A CUSTOMS OFFICIALS, R50,000 TO A SARS OFFICIAL, R120,000 AND R5000 FOR COPS…
In early 2011, SARS swooped in, arresting Carim for customs fraud. SARS then REFUSED to give Carim and Kajee a manufacturing licence for their new factory in Pietermaritzburg. While Carim was trying to clear his name with SARS, Kajee changed company documents, ejecting Carim as a director from the factory and changing its name to ATM. Edward Zuma became its sole director.
X: Then when Edward Zuma becomes the director, the factory gets granted a manufacturing licence from SARS.
With license in hand, Zuma resigned, handing the company back to Kajee.
Snykers: Now we know that Edward Zuma has since left although there are indications that he's potentially still a silent partner in the business.
Edward Zuma said we should send our questions to his partner Kajee: upsound: it shows they still do business. He laughed when we asked him about the payments. “Laughs...absurd… no idea what you’re talking about. Later alleging that we’ve been paid by BAT to make these “ridiculous” claims.
Kajee’s former business partner Carim said : “Unfortunately I'm unable to comment as the investigation is ongoing. I can confirm my companies were hijacked by Mr Yusuf Kajee.”
Kajee denies hijacking ATM.
KAJEE: the state prosecutor threw this whole case out of court saying that this was a vendetta. I ended up paying SARS and signed an indemnity with them that I would not make the case public.
S: Have you ever smuggled? Yes or no.
K: Me? Smuggled? Smuggled what?
S: Cigarettes obviously.
K: I’ve smuggled a few white girls in my room.
S: I think you should answer the questions rather than be funny.K: I've never smuggled cigarettes. Who the fuck is carte blanche in my life?He warned our producer that the industry wouldn’t be happy with this story. K: They’ll eat you up for breakfast, You’ll lose your job.
Kajee later said players along the distribution chain are illegally selling cigarettes from their storage facilities.


But it’s not just the smaller manufacturers who have questions to answer. With 30-billion Rands of South African government pension funds invested in BAT, the tobacco industry wields enormous power.
Snyckers: British American Tobacco in particular they have a very long history internationally of their packs ending up on the black market.
BAT has two outstanding tax bills, to the tune of R2,2-billion, unrelated to smuggling, that they’re disputing with SARS.

Van Loggernberg says in 2014 SARS was about to audit all the cigarette manufacturers when the tobacco industry hit back.
A false narrative was created with the sole purpose of discrediting Van Loggernberg and his SARS unit by calling them “rogue agents.” This was fed to the media including Carte Blanche. It resulted in Van Loggerenberg leaving SARS, undermining its investigative capabilities, as well as halting investigations into the tobacco manufacturers.
M: So there was never a rogue unit?
Snyckers: There was never a rogue unit.
Van Loggernberg and and his unit members were only just vindicated this June, when the report by the inspector general of intelligence ONE OF THOSE that had been used to discredit them in 2014 was finally reviewed and set aside.
JVL: The Inspector General of Intelligence has given me Their assurance that they will be investigating.
Van Loggerenberg has published the court documents which had formed part of his investigations at SARS before he left. These BAT internal emails show that BAT had paid a lawyer 3000 pounds a month for privileged information on its competitors. That cash was withdrawn locally via these travelex cards.

BAT has never responded to these allegations and declined an interview now, saying it would only promote books written by Van Loggerenberg and Snyckers.

Their latest media statement denies involvement in any smuggling saying:

“BAT south africa exports to 12 other countries and the volumes we are producing are consistent with export volumes before the lockdown.

“BAT south africa is working closely with SARS and have implemented new processes and protocols for production and export.”

They say: “We have SARS officials at our factory who are controlling production volumes, auditing the export declarations, verifying the container loading and sealing the containers.”

“If the country is to capture any of the taxes it so desperately needs then SARS needs to be allocated the required resources to establish a nationwide task force.”

SARS declined to comment, saying it could not make private tax matters public.
The Government has said the sale of cigarettes will only be allowed under level 2 of lockdown…this has inflamed many smokers who protested the ban. UPSOUND?
Van Loggernberg believes the only way forward is for the government and SARS to continue with the investigations he had begun into the tobacco industry.

Snyckers: British American Tobacco in particular they have a very long history internationally of their packs ending up on the black market. BAT has two outstanding tax bills, to the tune of R2,2-billion, unrelated to smuggling, that they’re disputing with SARS. Van Loggernberg says in 2014 SARS was about to audit all the cigarette manufacturers when the tobacco industry hit back. A false narrative was created with the sole purpose of discrediting Van Loggernberg and his SARS unit by calling them “rogue agents.” This was fed to the media including Carte Blanche. It resulted in Van Loggerenberg leaving SARS, undermining its investigative capabilities, as well as halting investigations into the tobacco manufacturers. M: So there was never a rogue unit? Snyckers: There was never a rogue unit. Van Loggernberg and and his unit members were only just vindicated this June, when the report by the inspector general of intelligence ONE OF THOSE that had been used to discredit them in 2014 was finally reviewed and set aside. JVL: The Inspector General of Intelligence has given me Their assurance that they will be investigating. Van Loggerenberg has published the court documents which had formed part of his investigations at SARS before he left. These BAT internal emails show that BAT had paid a lawyer 3000 pounds a month for privileged information on its competitors. That cash was withdrawn locally via these travelex cards. BAT has never responded to these allegations and declined an interview now, saying it would only promote books written by Van Loggerenberg and Snyckers. Their latest media statement denies involvement in any smuggling saying: “BAT south africa exports to 12 other countries and the volumes we are producing are consistent with export volumes before the lockdown. “BAT south africa is working closely with SARS and have implemented new processes and protocols for production and export.” They say: “We have SARS officials at our factory who are controlling production volumes, auditing the export declarations, verifying the container loading and sealing the containers.” “If the country is to capture any of the taxes it so desperately needs then SARS needs to be allocated the required resources to establish a nationwide task force.” SARS declined to comment, saying it could not make private tax matters public. The Government has said the sale of cigarettes will only be allowed under level 2 of lockdown…this has inflamed many smokers who protested the ban. UPSOUND? Van Loggernberg believes the only way forward is for the government and SARS to continue with the investigations he had begun into the tobacco industry.
